name: driftwood balance sheet — the risk book priced as Total Cost of Risk
note: One row per open risk. Each row's triples feed the FAIR £; each row's costs let the war-gamer weigh fix vs cage vs transfer vs deny and book the cheapest. warn = do-nothing exposure, deny = loss path closed (~0), behind = the residual a cage would collapse (defaults to warn). costs in GBP/yr; transfer.load = insurer margin over expected loss, transfer.deductible = the slice you keep. Triples (min,mode,max), events/yr.

risks.name: unversioned image ships cart PII
risks.note: Cheap to remediate (bump the image, re-pin the version) -> FIX wins the crossover.

risks.name: legacy checkout on a past-EOL runtime, cannot be patched in place
risks.note: Fixing means a rewrite (ruinous); denying kills live revenue -> a CAGE is cheapest, and its run-cost lands on cost-of-controls.

risks.name: third-party fulfilment integration, exposure outside our remediation reach
risks.note: Not a workload we admit, so fix/cage/deny don't apply -> only TRANSFER: cede it to a carrier, keep the deductible.
